articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Sunyshore needs long possessions against Mossdeep’s fast scoring
articles.dek: The Starseekers bring two playoff wins and Myles Gabite’s rushing production to a rematch of their 27–3 regular-season loss.

body.text: Mossdeep and Sunyshore reach the conference championship with a clear difference in how their latest wins developed. The Eclipse scored touchdowns on their first three possessions against Dewford and won 40–3. The Starseekers protected a four-point halftime lead against Petalburg, intercepted a third-quarter threat and finished the game through their rushing attack. Both approaches worked. Sunyshore now has to make its approach survive against the league's strongest full-season scoring record.

Mossdeep finished the regular season 17–0, with 724 points scored and 130 allowed. Sunyshore finished 13–4, scoring 423 and conceding 211. Those remain regular-season records; the Eclipse have added one playoff win after their bye, while the Starseekers have added two. The teams' Week 16 meeting ended 27–3 to Mossdeep. That is direct matchup evidence, although the new game will have its own possessions and a different availability picture.

Marshall Flock's new two-week injury entry is the most immediate personnel change for the home team. Poury Holt remains listed for four weeks. Sunyshore's 88 Special remains at fourteen. The available record does not announce replacement assignments, so the preview cannot promise a particular defender will inherit Flock's work. It can identify the absence and ask whether the Starseekers' passing game can make that change consequential.
Gabite has supplied a reliable beginning

Myles Gabite rushed for 106 yards against Hearthome and 134 against Petalburg. His combined playoff total is 240 yards, and he carried nineteen times in the divisional win. Sunyshore gained 177 rushing yards as a team against the Pride, including Kobra Khan's twenty-nine and Jolt Vick's eleven. The rushing attack gave Karson Jones more than one contributor, with Gabite providing the largest sustained workload.

The closing possession against Petalburg shows the value of that production in a precise situation. Gabite gained twelve yards at the two-minute mark, then fourteen on third-and-seven with 1:51 remaining. Sunyshore finished with kneel-downs. Those carries ended the opponent's opportunity to respond, protecting a 24–10 lead without requiring another pass into a defense that had already intercepted DeZhaun Watzon once and sacked him four times.

Creating that situation against Mossdeep is substantially harder. Dewford managed thirty rushing yards in the divisional game, with Excadrill gaining twenty-seven on ten carries. The Breakers fell behind early and could not maintain a useful rushing answer. Sunyshore's better recent ground production gives it a stronger starting argument, but the Eclipse have just demonstrated how quickly an opponent can lose the option of playing at its preferred pace.

The Starseekers need first downs early enough to make Gabite's carries part of competitive possessions. A five-yard gain while trailing by one score can support the next decision. The same gain while several touchdowns behind consumes time without sufficiently reducing the deficit. That is a game-state distinction, not a prediction that Sunyshore should abandon the run after one difficult series. Its most productive offensive player needs enough opportunities to influence the score.
Watzon's protection is an immediate concern

Watzon completed eleven of eighteen passes for 111 yards, two touchdowns and one interception against Petalburg. Delcatty sacked him three times and Kabutops once. Sunyshore still won because it finished two early touchdown drives, recovered from the interception through its defense and kept rushing effectively. Those successful recoveries should not obscure the cost of four sacks in a relatively small passing workload.

Mossdeep's pass rush has just recorded five sacks, led by Derrat Brooks with three. Joey Sporeter and Bearon Donald added one each. The home defense also intercepted Dewford once through Luvrelle Revis. If the Eclipse create the same combination of lost yardage and a takeaway, Watzon will be asked to recover possessions against an offense capable of scoring before Sunyshore gets another extended opportunity.

The Starseekers' early touchdown passes against Petalburg were short finishes: five yards to Fera LaGatr on fourth-and-five and two to EKTRIK RED. Those conversions demonstrate that Watzon can complete an important possession even when the broader passing total is modest. Against Mossdeep, the challenge begins before those finishing downs. Sunyshore must reach scoring range often enough that the short touchdown options can affect the game.

Flock's absence gives the visitors a specific defensive change to examine, but it does not establish an automatic passing advantage. Marino's team still has a productive rush and other established defenders. Sunyshore will need to show that a receiving opportunity actually exists through completions, rather than treating the injury list as an extra touchdown already assigned to its side of the scoreboard.
Ninjaskamara forces several kinds of defense

Ninjaskamara produced 279 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns against Dewford. He rushed for 189 yards on twenty carries and caught two passes for ninety yards, with both receptions scoring. His sixty-six-yard receiving touchdown came on third-and-eight. Sunyshore cannot evaluate him only as a runner it wants to tackle near the line; he has just converted an apparent passing down into the longest touchdown of the game.

The Starseekers allowed Petalburg thirty-eight rushing yards. That is encouraging, following the nineteen they allowed Hearthome in the wild-card round. Ninjaskamara presents a different level of recent production, supported by an offense that also gained fifty-eight rushing yards from Shawn Mareman against Dewford. Mossdeep can continue running productively when its leading back is not taking every carry.

Marino completed sixteen of twenty-two passes for 242 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. Accel BeckhmJr caught six passes for ninety-one yards and a touchdown. Those numbers explain why dedicating attention to the backfield does not solve the entire matchup. Sunyshore has to limit Ninjaskamara while preserving enough coverage and pressure to prevent Marino from finding Accel repeatedly on productive downs.

Ash Rothington's three sacks against Petalburg offer one concrete route to interruption. Each sack cost the Pride seven yards. The Starseekers also intercepted Iron Valiant through Scol Alexander after their own turnover had given Petalburg a chance to take the lead. Sunyshore has evidence of defensive responses under pressure. It now needs those responses against a quarterback who avoided turnovers throughout his divisional performance.
Early scoring will shape the available choices

Mossdeep's first three drives against Dewford covered seventy-four, sixty-six and eighty-three yards, each ending in a touchdown. The Eclipse did not depend on a sequence of gifts near the goal line to establish their lead. That matters for Sunyshore's preparation because simply protecting the ball may not be enough. The Starseekers need stops on possessions that begin with a full field available to Marino.

Sunyshore can take some confidence from its own opening work against Petalburg. Its first two touchdown possessions covered sixty-four and seventy-two yards. Watzon and Gabite therefore have recent evidence of moving the ball through complete drives, even with a limited final passing total. Repeating that movement would keep Mossdeep's offense waiting and prevent the first quarter from becoming a sequence of immediate home scoring opportunities.

Third downs will be particularly revealing. Petalburg converted five of ten against Sunyshore, while the Starseekers converted two of six and also finished the fourth-and-five touchdown. The final result favored Sunyshore because of what happened after those conversions and on the ground. Against Mossdeep, repeatedly conceding manageable extensions could expose the defense to too many additional touches from Ninjaskamara and Accel.

The kicking details also deserve a place in a close-game scenario. Vinathorn missed two extra points against Dewford, finishing four-for-six. Sunyshore made a forty-two-yard field goal through Kayden Lyons to extend its lead after Alexander's interception. These facts do not establish how either kicker will perform next week. They identify recent execution that can matter if the stronger offense does not create its usual separation.
The path to an upset and the forecast

Sunyshore's upset case begins with Gabite sustaining drives, Rothington helping force a punt or a difficult conversion, and Watzon protecting the possessions those efforts create. It also requires the Starseekers to finish with touchdowns more frequently than Dewford managed. Field goals can keep a score respectable; Mossdeep's demonstrated touchdown production makes them a difficult foundation for winning an entire game.

Mossdeep's favored case is broader. Marino can move the ball through several receivers, Ninjaskamara can score as a runner or receiver, Mareman can support the rushing workload, and the defense has just limited an opponent to 122 total yards. Flock's absence narrows the available defensive options, but the current evidence still gives the Eclipse more independently demonstrated ways to create a scoring advantage.

My forecast is Mossdeep 35, Sunyshore 17. I expect the Starseekers to generate more offense than they did in the 27–3 regular-season meeting, especially through Gabite's recent form, while Mossdeep's receiving depth and ability to turn third downs into large gains produce the decisive separation. Sunyshore has earned another attempt at the top seed; the Eclipse enter that attempt with the stronger case in both recent production and the complete season.
